subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should the public cron run contract change so all CLI/RPC/manual runs preserve scheduler state and delete-after-run one-shots, with only the gateway on-exit watcher retaining a private consuming path?
rationale: This is a deliberate compatibility change for existing public manual-run callers, not a purely mechanical correction; source confirms current main uses one finalization behavior for public and watcher force runs.

options.title: Adopt non-consuming public runs
options.body: Confirm operator-only public cron runs, retain the private watcher-terminal entry point, and require final-head live proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve consuming manual force runs
options.body: Keep current public force-run semantics and close or substantially redesign the PR around an explicit opt-in verification mode instead.

recommendation.title: Adopt non-consuming public runs
recommendation.body: Confirm operator-only public cron runs, retain the private watcher-terminal entry point, and require final-head live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the adjacent next-run preservation and maintenance invariants affected by this contract choice.
